original.target_description: Recall of associated backgrounds for emotional versus neutral items. Experiment and precise test unresolved: study_o is null and the p. 6 locator cannot be mapped to the unpaginated supplied text. Both experiments report relevant recall analyses.

n.sample_role: Unassigned candidates: Experiment 1 background-recall group explicitly has 18 participants; Experiment 2 reports 45 participants in Participants, retained as recruitment/contributor candidate only.
n.exclusions: No exclusions stated in the inspected participant, procedure and recall-results sections. No final analytic N inferred from df.
n.quote: In the background recall test, participants ( N =18) were presented with items from previously-studied scenes and were asked to recall the associated background, by typing a brief description. ... Forty-five Wofford College students (20 women, ages 18 to 22, M = 20.79, SD = 1.19) participated for course credit or a $50 raffle.

p.quote: There also was a main effect of Valence, F (2,33) = 11.02, p <.001, η P 2 =.40 ... there was also a significant main effect of Valence, F (2,88)=24.032, p <.001, η P 2 =.353 ... For First Cues, items were most likely to trigger background memory if the cues were negative (vs. neutral: t (44)=6.247, p <.001; vs. positive: t (44)=3.158, p =.003) and positive cues were more effective than neutral ( t (44)=3.842, p <.001).

notes: Identity assessment: supplied header matches Neutral Details Associated with Emotional Events are Encoded: Evidence from a Cued Recall Paradigm; Katherine R Mickley Steinmetz, Aubrey G Knight, Elizabeth A Kensinger; DOI 10.1080/02699931.2015.1059317. Primary author manuscript in PMC, final edited publication Cognition and Emotion 30(7), 1352–1360. The canonical web parse contains both experiments, methods, results, general discussion and references, rather than only an abstract. No PDF supplied; unpaginated text does not establish the p. 6 mapping. All assigned fields inspected together. The neutral description does not distinguish Experiment 1 versus Experiment 2, omnibus valence versus item-cue-specific contrast, or positive versus neutral versus negative versus neutral. No assignment by row order or numeric matching. Candidate N: Experiment 1 explicitly assigns 18 participants to the background recall test; Experiment 2 reports 45 participants in Participants, not promoted to final analytic N. Printed candidates: Experiment 1 recall main Valence F (2,33) = 11.02, p <.001, partial eta-squared .40; Experiment 2 recall main Valence F (2,88)=24.032, p <.001, partial eta-squared .353; Experiment 2 Cue Type by Valence F (2,88)=18.362, p <.001, partial eta-squared .294. These are different tests and the main effects span both cue types. Experiment 1 follow-ups across cue types: positive>neutral t (35) = 1.945, p = .06; negative>neutral t (35) = 4.656, p <.001. Experiment 2 item-cue First Cue: negative versus neutral t (44)=6.247, p <.001; positive versus neutral t (44)=3.842, p <.001. Second Cue: negative versus neutral t (44)=5.276, p <.001. No conversion to requested partial eta-squared, no N derived from df, and no N sum. All target values remain null with confidence false. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
